samples.summary: Report asserts "narrowed by the verifiers" without any check that the scoped title is actually narrower
samples.evidence: renderUiReport emits `> The hunter proposed this as **"${k.title}"** — narrowed by the verifiers to the heading above.` whenever `c.scopedTitle && c.scopedTitle !== k.title`. Difference is not narrowing: a verifier may supply a scopedTitle that is broader, differently scoped, or names a different mechanism than the hunter's title, and the report will still state that it was narrowed. Nothing in `uiScopedTitle` (hunt-ui.mjs:286-291) or the gate compares breadth. The one line a maintainer reads is therefore accompanied by a claim the pipeline never established.

samples.summary: When no verifier supplies a scopedTitle, the overclaimed hunter title is headlined with no signal that the narrowing step failed
samples.evidence: `return scoped[0] ?? claimed?.title ?? "(untitled)";` falls back to the explorer's title. In that case `record.scopedTitle === k.title`, so renderUiReport (line 781) prints no note, and `record.overclaimed` — which may be true from the very same verdicts (uiOverclaimed, line 294) — is never rendered per finding; only the aggregate `stats.overclaimed` line at 1064 exists. The report then presents a title the verifiers explicitly flagged as overclaiming as if it were the bounded claim, which is exactly the failure the change exists to prevent.

samples.summary: Only the first verifier's scopedTitle is used; disagreement between verifiers is silently discarded
samples.evidence: `uiScopedTitle` maps all verdicts but returns `scoped[0]`. With `persona.verifiers >= 2` (gate requires >= 2 confirmations), a second verifier that bounded the defect much more narrowly, or that named a different mechanism, is dropped without any record of the disagreement. Unlike `groundedIn` (uiCitationsOf), which unions verifier-supplied evidence, this takes an arbitrary single opinion and presents it in the heading as "the verifiers'" claim (report line 771-774, 782).

samples.summary: stats.overclaimed only counts REPORTED findings, so the documented "drift toward overclaiming" signal misses most of the population
samples.evidence: `if (record.overclaimed) stats.overclaimed++;` sits inside the `isFilingVerdict(...)` true branch only. Candidates refuted or capped never contribute, even though verifiers were run on the refuted ones (line 1337-1346) and their `overclaimed` flags exist in `verdicts`. The comment at 1124-1128 claims the counter makes systemic overclaiming visible; it only measures the small subset that passed the gate, so a rising overclaiming rate among refuted candidates is invisible.

samples.summary: Heading uses `??`, so an empty-string scopedTitle yields an empty heading, inconsistent with the truthiness test one line below
samples.evidence: `const heading = c.scopedTitle ?? k.title;` treats `""` as present, producing `### [major] ` with no title, while line 781 (`c.scopedTitle && ...`) treats `""` as absent and suppresses the note. `uiScopedTitle` cannot currently return `""` unless `claimed.title` is `""`, but renderUiReport is exported and also fed records round-tripped through the findings JSON written at line 1038, so the two guards should agree; use truthiness in both.

samples.summary: Verifier-supplied scopedTitle is interpolated into a Markdown `###` heading without newline/markdown sanitisation
samples.evidence: `### [${k.severity}] ${heading}` places raw model prose on a heading line. A scopedTitle containing a newline splits the heading and the remainder renders as body text (or as a forged `##` section if it starts with `#`), unlike the drop table at line 832 which at least escapes `|` and truncates. Pre-existing for `k.title`, but the heading now comes from a second, differently prompted model.
